memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Ordinary trip-specific evaluation of elapsed time, connections, baggage costs, and destination time. The user selected the later-return nonstop pairing for this San Diego trip; no durable travel preference was established.

messages.content: Can you put the three San Diego flight combinations side by side? I want the real elapsed times, connection details, bag charges, and how much time we'd actually have there. Our combined airfare cap is $1,150 for the two of us.

Yes. The $1,086 nonstop pairing departs MSP Friday at 9:20 a.m., arrives SAN at 11:18 a.m., and takes 3 hours 58 minutes. Wednesday's nonstop leaves SAN at 12:40 p.m., reaches MSP at 6:10 p.m., and takes 3 hours 30 minutes. That gives you 97 hours 22 minutes in San Diego between arrival and departure.
And the cheaper one-stop? The late Friday arrival worries me more than the connection itself.

The $914 pairing leaves MSP Friday at 12:10 p.m., connects in Denver for 1 hour 12 minutes, and reaches SAN at 8:08 p.m. Total outbound elapsed time is 9 hours 58 minutes. Its Wednesday return leaves at 10:45 a.m., has a 58-minute Denver connection, and arrives MSP at 6:55 p.m.; elapsed time is 6 hours 10 minutes. You would have 86 hours 37 minutes at the destination, about 10 hours 45 minutes less than with the $1,086 nonstops.
That effectively wipes out Friday. What exactly do we gain with the $1,142 option?

It uses the same Friday nonstop, 9:20 a.m. to 11:18 a.m., but moves Wednesday's nonstop to 5:35 p.m., arriving MSP at 11:03 p.m. The return takes 3 hours 28 minutes. That produces 102 hours 17 minutes in San Diego, which is 4 hours 55 minutes more than the $1,086 pairing and 15 hours 40 minutes more than the one-stop itinerary.
So the late return is still under $1,150, but barely.
Correct. At $1,142 total for both travelers, it is $8 under the airfare ceiling. It costs $56 more than the earlier nonstop pairing and $228 more than the one-stop pairing.
Now include the luggage. We may each check one suitcase, and I don't want the displayed fare to hide that.

All three displayed fares include advance standard-seat selection but exclude checked bags. The first checked bag is $35 per person each way, so two travelers checking one bag apiece would add $140 round trip. Totals including those bags would be $1,226 for the earlier nonstops, $1,054 for the one-stop pairing, and $1,282 for the later-return nonstops.
The $1,150 limit is airfare before bags, so that's okay. Are either of those Denver connections especially risky or rushed?

The 1-hour-12-minute outbound connection is workable under the posted schedule and leaves some margin. The 58-minute return connection is legal but tighter: a delay into Denver could make the second flight difficult, and checked bags would need to transfer. The nonstop choices remove both connection points and shorten total travel time substantially.
For five nights, I don't think saving $228 is worth losing most of Friday and adding two connections. Between the nonstop choices, quantify what the extra $56 buys us.

The extra $56 buys 4 hours 55 minutes more in San Diego on Wednesday. It leaves enough time for breakfast, a coastal morning, and lunch before heading to the airport, whereas the 12:40 p.m. departure would make Wednesday mainly a checkout-and-airport day. The tradeoff is reaching Minneapolis at 11:03 p.m. instead of 6:10 p.m.
Choose the $1,142 nonstop round trip, then. Keep it unbooked until we settle the hotel split, but tell me the exact flight decision and what needs rechecking.

Selected, not booked: Friday, October 4, nonstop MSP-SAN from 9:20 a.m. to 11:18 a.m.; Wednesday, October 9, nonstop SAN-MSP from 5:35 p.m. to 11:03 p.m. Airfare is $1,142 for two, $8 below the airfare cap. If both of you check one bag each way, the expected flight total becomes $1,282. Before purchase, recheck fare availability, the exact bag fee, seat-selection terms, operating carrier, and whether either flight time has changed. This pairing preserves 102 hours 17 minutes at the destination and fits the five-night plan.
